**Do you want to help ensure quality in energy infrastructure projects? Can you turn quality requirements into practical activities and support projects through to handover? And do you have experience with quality management, audits and inspections? Then join COWI as our new Quality Consultant.

****Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

**We are looking for a Quality Consultant to join COWI and support our customers’ construction and operational projects on assignments of both shorter and longer duration. You will help ensure that projects follow the customer’s governance framework and can be handed over to the operations organisation at the required quality level, with all supporting documentation. Your work may span electricity transmission projects, including cables, overhead lines and substations; gas distribution and transmission networks, including natural gas and biogas facilities and stations; oil pipelines; and gas storage facilities.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Support projects in applying internal processes and tools and provide guidance and support on quality-related matters.

• Consistently promote and embed quality management in projects so that documentation, products and deliverables meet the specified requirements

• Plan, carry out and document the necessary quality activities in collaboration with the project team, including internal and external audits and inspections of project partners.

• Ensure that quality-related experience and lessons learned are shared within the customer’s organisation.

• Prepare project quality plans.

**Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

**The first step to success in this role is that you are eager to collaborate with the people around you, whether they are colleagues, partners or customers. Developing ties with others is something you do by acting respectfully and delivering on your promises. And you never get set in your ways, but keep exploring new insights and ways to improve.

You work in a structured and systematic way and take a proactive approach to building relationships. You collaborate and communicate on an equal footing with internal and external stakeholders involved in construction projects. You bring professional credibility in your field and can work independently.

On top of that, you will have:

• An understanding of the structure and application of quality management systems.

• Experience with project- and process-related work.

• Experience with quality management activities in infrastructure and construction projects, including quality assurance (QA) and providing input to quality control (QC) activities.

• Experience carrying out quality activities, including audits and inspections of internal and external parties involved in projects.

• Experience using the Microsoft Office suite.

• The ability to communicate in Danish and English, both orally and in writing, at negotiation level.

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarters in Lyngby.

**A place to work and so much more

**At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

**Before you apply

**All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

**Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key

**We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports
 Faculty of Science
 University of Copenhagen
 
 The Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports at the University of Copenhagen invites applications for a Professorship in Human Nutrition and Health. 

  We seek a colleague who brings strong scientific leadership, a collaborative spirit, and a deep commitment to advancing research and education in human nutrition and health. The candidate will be joining a dynamic and interdisciplinary department dedicated to excellence in research, teaching and societal impact

  The ideal candidate will have:

   	
• A strong track record of shaping state-of-the-art knowledge in human nutrition, with documented impact on mechanistic understanding of nutritional impact on human health. 	
• Extensive expertise in conducting clinical trials.  	
• Solid teaching and supervisor experience at university level (BSc, MSc and PhD). 	
• An excellent publication record within the area of human nutrition and health.  	
• Proven ability to attract competitive national and international research funding. 	
• A forward looking, realistic 5-year research plan, including clear milestones that demonstrate how your work will enrich and expand the departments experimental research profile.   We particularly welcome applicants excited about strengthening our interdisciplinary research environment.

  The ideal candidate should have:

   	
• Documented teaching competencies and must be able to explain and reflect upon their own teaching practice and portfolio.  	
• Formal pedagogical training and supervision equivalent to the University of Copenhagen teacher training programme. 	
• Strong leadership and management skills.    The ideal candidate’s responsibilities will include:

   	
• Conducting cutting-edge research and contributing to the continued development of the research area. 	
• Applying for competitive grants and leading research projects. 	
• Supervising, mentoring and training of research fellows and other staff. 	
• Contributing actively to teaching, curriculum development, supervision, examinations and other tasks requested by the Department including administrative academic duties. 	
• Strengthening the Departments mission to deliver research and research-based education at the highest international level.    The candidate will become part of an inspiring and diverse academic community. The research of the department is broad and includes basic physiology, human movement and exercise science, humanities related to exercise and sport as well as diet and nutrition science. 

  Assessment of applicants will primarily consider their level of documented, original scientific production at an international level, including contributions to developments in their field, as well as their documented teaching qualifications. Managerial and out-reach qualifications of applicants including ability to attract external funding will also be considered.

  General criteria apply to the appointment of professors at the University of Copenhagen. The criteria (research, teaching, innovation and societal impact, organizational contributionand leadership) are considered as a framework for an overall assessment of the applicant. In addition, each applicant will be assessed according to the specific requirements listed in this advertisement. 

  Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen’s Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact here.

  Further information about the Department can be found at Department of Nutrition, Exercise and Sports – University of Copenhagen (ku.dk)

  Potential applicants are encouraged to seek further information by contacting Head of Department, Professor Nikolai B. Nordsborg (nbn@nexs.ku.dk; +45 28751612).

  The position is open from 1 May 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect on the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

There will be an opportunity to negotiate supplements based on qualifications. You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

The Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme (NQCP) is expanding its talented and international team to add to its cutting-edge quantum programme in the heart of Copenhagen, Denmark. At the Niels Bohr Institute, University of Copenhagen, we are running an international quantum computing programme, funded by the Novo Nordisk Foundation, that drives research and innovations at multiple levels - from developing scalable quantum processor technologies to quantum algorithms and applications.  The long-term mission of the programme is to develop fault-tolerant quantum computing hardware and quantum algorithms that solve life-science-relevant chemical and biological problems.

  Start date is the 1st of February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter. 

  The project 
 The position is centred on the development of integrated superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors (SNSPDs) embedded in controllable photonic circuits for the fully integrated processing of the emitted photons from silicon quantum emitters. The work will be performed as part of the Photonic Control and Readout team in NQCP, in close collaboration with the Theory & Simulation and the Materials engineering teams at NQCP and the Growth team at Quantum Foundry. These teams will support the efforts of the development and integration of SNSPDs in our photonic circuit.

  You will be collaborating closely with the other team members of the Photonic C&R team and – like the rest of the team - be generally involved in the projects related to the platform. A number of students will also be dedicated to the SNSPD projects. The nanofabrication is done at the DTU Nanolab – a 1,350 m² ISO 4–6 cleanroom with over 150 state-of-the-art tools, and one of the leading cleanrooms in Europe. Testing and integration of the SNSPDs will be done at the NQCP Photonics lab at the Niels Bohr Institute established in 2023. The lab contains a range of cryostats (mK to 4K) designed for optical fibre access, state-of-the-art electronics, commercial SNSPDs, etc.

  The position is also open as an assistant professor. Please apply to the call corresponding to the position relevant for you.

  Responsibilities:

   	
• Taking the leading role in developing and integrating SNSPDs into our photonic circuits and establishing the electrical control circuit. 	
• Structuring the efforts on multiple projects, integrating experimental results in our database, and providing feedback to collaborating teams. 	
• Contributing to the other projects within the Photonics team. The projects span single photon sources and optical components like switches, cavities, etc. 	
• Teaching and supervision of students. 	
• Procurement, maintenance, and operation of scientific equipment.    

  We are looking for the following qualifications: 

   	
• PhD with postdoc experience in experimental physics, engineering, nanotechnologies, or related. 	
• Experience with SNSPDs fabrication and characterisation, quantum photonics, electronics, and cryogenic systems. 	
• Experience with control software and data logging – preferably in python.   Good communication skills and a structured approach to work.
 
 Why Us? 
 Joining NQCP now, you will get involved in a well-established and ambitious programme, which offers excellent opportunities to build a career in advancing quantum computing. We want to make Denmark a world leader in quantum research, and we hope to attract people from all over the world.  

   

  Life in Denmark is supported with strong social services (free universal healthcare, free/subsidised language courses, paid parental leave, subsidised day care institutions and excellent public schools). Our work culture is very egalitarian and prioritises work life balance. Dual career families are the norm, and workplaces offer flexibility to support everyone in having both an exciting career and good family time. Danish cities are known for having excellent infrastructure, for example through widespread bike path networks. We can also offer a thriving food-scene, excellent museums, and beautiful natural scenery. 

   

  Further information on the Department is linked at Novo Nordisk Foundation Quantum Computing Programme – University of Copenhagen, Inquiries about the position can be made to Stefano Paesani: stefano.paesani@nbi.ku.dk or Peter Granum: peter.granum@nbi.ku.dk.

 The position is covered by the Memorandum on Job Structure for Academic Staff.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State.

  Negotiation for salary supplement is possible.

  Appointment will be subject to receipt of a security clearance.
 
 The position is open from 1 February 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.
 
 The position is limited in time to 2 years from the date of employment with possible extension. The duration can be negotiated.

  The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background
  

  You can read more about salary levels in the state sector www.loenoverblik.dk (in Danish).

  When you will be affiliated with the University of Copenhagen or otherwise have access to their research, you may be required to undergo a background screening. The purpose is to protect the security and research integrity of the University of Copenhagen.

  
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically.

  Please include 

   	
• Motivation letter (max. one page)      	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position      	
• Original PhD diploma and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish.     	
• Publication list    	
• Reference letters   The deadline for applications is 24th of November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We will call for interviews shortly after the application deadline. Interviews are expected to take place in mid-December or early-January.

Project Manager

Your impact begins here

As Project Manager in Production Support Aseptic Manufacturing, you will take ownership of a portfolio of production projects in Hillerød that needs more hands. You will drive IT, equipment and validation projects from start to finish, helping new products reach production, processes run better and compliance stay strong.

This is a 12-month parental leave cover, with real responsibility from the start. Your work helps the site supply people living with serious chronic diseases.

What you’ll bring

As a Project Manager in our Production Support Aseptic Manufacturing department, you will independently drive projects throughout their entire lifecycle within a production environment that is scaling rapidly to meet growing global demand. The portfolio is expanding, the challenges are complex, and the impact is real.

• A master’s degree in engineering, pharmaceutical sciences or another relevant field.

• Around 4–5 years of professional experience.

• Evidence of strong stakeholder management, communication, leadership and governance.

• Structure and ownership: you plan carefully, work to defined processes and timelines, and follow through on what you commit to.

• The ability to use PowerPoint and Excel to present project timelines, build scenarios and support stakeholder decisions.

• Professional proficiency in English.

Useful, but not essential:

• Experience as a Project Manager or in a similar coordinating role.

• Experience from a GMP-regulated environment, including aseptic or finished production.

• Experience with IT-related projects.

What you’ll do

You will keep a busy production project portfolio moving, so the people who run the site can focus on supplying treatments.

• Drive projects independently through their full lifecycle, from initiation to completion, in an aseptic and finished production environment.

• Plan, run and follow up on scope, schedule, resources, cost, quality and risk.

• Lead projects across IT, equipment and validation, driven by new product introductions, optimisation and compliance requirements.

• Present timelines and scenarios clearly, so stakeholders can make timely decisions.

• Stay in close dialogue with line of business, site management at all levels and external vendors to keep everyone aligned.

Who you’ll work with

You will join the Project Management Office (PMO) in Production Support Aseptic Manufacturing, part of Drug Product Manufacturing within Global Manufacturing & Supply. The PMO is a team of more than 40 Project Managers running small to large projects across the Hillerød site. These cover aseptic production (formulation, filling and inspection), finished production (assembly and packaging), IT, material handling systems and building facilities.

You will work every day with line of business, site management and external vendors. Global Manufacturing & Supply spans the value chain from drug and device development to marketed Novo products, and your projects are part of how the site scales to reach more people. You will cover for a colleague on leave, so you will work closely with your PMO colleagues to pick up the portfolio and keep projects on track.

What you can expect here

You will be trusted to take ownership and make your voice heard. Your projects will be varied, so you will build new skills across IT, equipment and validation, and learn alongside experienced colleagues in the PMO. We value clear expectations, honest feedback and results, so you will know what good looks like and be recognised for delivering it.

The role is a 12-month temporary position, based in Hillerød, Denmark.

What we offer

At Novo, you will join a global healthcare company with a distinctive culture and a strong track record. We offer continuous learning, career development and benefits tailored to your life and career stage.

Salary: The annual base salary for this role ranges from DKK 570,200 to DKK 838,100, depending on the level of the position. Placement within the range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge and relevant experience.

Incentives and benefits: The compensation package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives, together with other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

Start now

Your impact begins today. If you are ready to take ownership of production projects that help bring treatments to more people, apply for the Project Manager role by 7 November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Product Marketing Manager - B2B Software for Manufacturers
jobs.description:
Highlights:

• Fast-growing B2B software platform with established global reach is looking for our first marketing hire.

• We have a broad, multi-product offering for a narrow industry, and we don't fit into a single existing "category box" as defined today -- giving you a meaty challenge to work with.

• We have large customers and touch a lot of users (as a platform for managing global supply-chains), so your work will be "heard around the world"

• We are a small, efficient, get-stuff-done team. Looking for someone who things that's the way to go.

About Supplios

Manufacturers live or die by their supply base. Sourcing the wrong supplier, onboarding one slowly, failing to qualify one properly or losing track of a non-conformance can stop a production line and cost millions. Yet most manufacturers still run these relationships across email chains, spreadsheets and shared drives.

Supplios is a supplier collaboration platform for manufacturers in automotive and industrial sectors. We cover the full supplier relationship: sourcing, onboarding, qualification, day-to-day collaboration, compliance and supplier quality — with a modern cloud based platform that is easy for manufacturers to implement and operate. It is built specifically for the way automotive and industrial manufacturers actually work.

We are headquartered in central Copenhagen and already serve customers globally in our vertical, including some of the most demanding names in automotive. We have grown to this point almost entirely on product strength, domain credibility and word of mouth. We have done very little marketing.

That is where you come in.

The role

This is our first marketing hire.

You will own positioning, messaging and sales enablement for a platform that already has real customers, real reference stories and real competitive wins — but no one whose job it is to articulate any of it. There is no existing playbook to inherit, no legacy brand guidelines to work around, and no committee to navigate. There is a large amount of low-hanging fruit and a clear runway to make a visible commercial impact within your first few months.

You will work directly and closely with our co-founder and CEO, who continues to run product. He knows the product and the domain deeply; what he needs is a strong product marketing partner to turn that into sharp positioning, messaging that lands with procurement, quality and operations buyers, and material that makes the sales conversation easier.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused role. You will be writing the copy, building the deck and updating the website — not briefing an agency to do it.

We work together from our office in central Copenhagen. This is primarily an in-office role: at this stage, and in this role in particular, the close working relationship with management & sales is much easier to build in person.

What you will do

• Own positioning and messaging for the Supplios platform and its individual modules, and make it consistent across every touchpoint

• Translate technical capability into buyer-relevant value for distinct personas — sourcing and procurement leads, supplier quality engineers, quality directors, supply chain and operations management

• Build the sales enablement layer: pitch decks, one-pagers, battlecards, demo narratives, proposal content and objection handling

• Run competitive and market intelligence, and keep the team honest about where we genuinely win and where we do not

• Plan and execute go-to-market for new modules and major releases, in step with the product roadmap

• Develop customer proof — case studies, reference stories and use cases — from an installed base that has plenty to say

• Rebuild our website messaging and product pages so they reflect what we actually do and who we do it for

• Feed structured market and customer insight back into product decisions

What we are looking for

Essential

• Proven product marketing experience in B2B or enterprise software, with responsibility for positioning, messaging and sales enablement

• A demonstrable track record of translating complex, technical products into clear commercial value propositions

• Excellent written English

• Comfort operating without a marketing team, an established playbook or a large budget — you scope the work, then do it

• The temperament for a small, senior, fast-moving company: high ownership, low ceremony

Nice to have

• Domain knowledge in automotive, industrial manufacturing or supply chain. Genuinely a plus, not a requirement. We can teach the domain to the right marketer; we cannot teach product marketing to a domain expert.

• Experience marketing to enterprise buyers with long, multi-stakeholder sales cycles

• Experience as an early marketing hire at a growing B2B software company

Language

• English is the only important language for this position — we work in English, and so do our customers. Danish language skills are not required.

Why this role is worth your time

• First marketing hire, not the fifth. You define how this company talks about itself.

• A product that already works. Real global customers in a demanding vertical, and reference stories waiting to be told.

• Work directly with the CEO/founders. No layers between you and the decisions.

• Visible impact. In a company that has barely marketed, good product marketing shows up in the pipeline quickly.

How to apply

Send your CV and a short note on why this role interests you to team@supplios.com. Work examples will help.

Apply by email

Send an email to team@supplios.com

Please include your CV / resume, and a brief note about why you're interested in the position.

Thanks!

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in Predictive Human Digital Twins for Human-Centred Systems Engineering – DTU Construct
jobs.description:
Are you interested in human-centred engineering at the intersection of biomechanics, artificial intelligence, and systems engineering, and want to build a strong methodological profile, this PhD position offers a unique opportunity – including the chance to help shape a new research group from the start.

At DTU Construct, you will develop methods that turn generic musculoskeletal models into personalised Human Digital Twins – based on sparse wearable sensor data instead of costly laboratory measurements or medical imaging – and assess how reliably they predict how a person moves and interacts with technical systems such as collaborative robots or assistive devices. The project is part of building up a new research group in Human-Centred Design within the Human-Centred Systems Engineering activities at DTU Construct. As part of the DTU PhD programme, you will follow PhD-level courses and contribute to teaching.

Responsibilities and qualifications
Your overall purpose will be to develop and validate methods for personalising biomechanical Human Digital Twins from sparse sensor data, combining physics-based and data-driven approaches and quantifying the gap between simulation and reality (sim2real).

Your primary tasks will be to:

• Develop methods for personalising musculoskeletal models from sparse multimodal sensor data.
• Combine physics-based and data-driven approaches for model calibration and prediction.
• Quantify and reduce the sim2real gap of Human Digital Twins.
• Plan and carry out experimental studies with human participants.
• Implement your methods in open, reusable software.
• Publish your results and collaborate with researchers at DTU and international partners.
We are looking for a motivated candidate with:

• An MSc in Biomedical or Mechanical Engineering, Robotics, Computer Science, Applied Mathematics, Engineering Design, or a related field.
• Solid programming skills (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++).
• A background in simulation, optimisation, machine learning, sensor processing, or parameter estimation.
• A strong interest in computational modelling of humans and human-technology systems.
• Good communication skills in English and the ability to work both independently and in a team.
• Experience with musculoskeletal modelling (e.g. OpenSim, AnyBody, SCONE), motion analysis, or wearable sensing is an advantage.
• We do not expect you to master all of these areas – a solid foundation and the motivation to grow into the field matter most.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Jörg Miehling.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

The period of employment is 3 years. Starting date is 1 March 2027 (or according to mutual agreement). The position is a full-time position.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information
Further information may be obtained from Jörg Miehling, jormi@dtu.dk (please mention “PhD Position Inquiry” in your email subject).

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk and the Section at www.construct.dtu.dk/sections/engineering-design-and-manufacturing-systems.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 2 December 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
• A copy of your BSc thesis (in pdf)
• A copy of your MSc thesis (in pdf)
• A copy of your scientific articles (if any) published so far (in pdf)
You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it. 

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. We undertake research, education, innovation, and scientific advice of the highest quality within building design and processes, building construction and safety, building energy and technical services, solid mechanics, fluid mechanics, coastal and maritime engineering, materials technology, manufacturing engineering, engineering systems design, design for sustainability, and thermal energy.

The Section of Engineering Design and Manufacturing Systems (EDM) advances the design of intelligent, resilient, and sustainable products and manufacturing systems, integrating systems engineering, modular architectures, robust and bio-inspired design, and AI-enabled engineering.

DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society. DTU has 13,800 students, 1,600 PhD students, and 6,500 employees. We work in an international environment and have an inclusive, stimulating, and informal work culture. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland and collaborates with the best universities around the world.

Do you have experience in managing complex operations contracts and commercial risk across countries? Do you enjoy building something into the next level?

We are looking for a Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to take end-to-end ownership of operations contracts across Eurowind Energy's global wind, solar and BESS portfolio.

Who we are

Eurowind Energy is a global and leading developer, owner and operator of energy parks. Based in Denmark, we operate in 16 countries around Europe and in the USA, and we are continuously growing our project portfolio. We believe in a future of renewable energy, and we have an ambitious plan of becoming the next generation's "Power Major". Based on a full value chain from greenfield project development to energy trading, more than 700 team members are dedicated to creating a greener future fueled with nothing but renewable energy!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Contract and Warranty Manager to join our Global Operations team. Based at our Operations office in Hobro, you will be the contract and warranty specialist for our global asset portfolio, supporting colleagues and managers across countries and functions.

Your role

As Senior Contract and Warranty Manager, you will take ownership of key commercial agreements, claims and warranty matters across Eurowind Energy's global asset portfolio. You will work closely with Asset Management, Operations, Finance, Legal and local teams to ensure that our contractual rights are understood, protected and actively used. The role combines hands-on contract management with a strong focus on risk, value creation and standardization across markets.

• Own contract management for operations contracts, including service and O&M agreements, warranty and performance guarantees, grid connection and curtailment compensation, insurance, land lease and supplier agreements

• Lead negotiation, drafting and execution of contracts so they meet both legal and commercial requirements

• Identify, assess and mitigate commercial and legal risk across the contract portfolio

• Manage claims and warranty follow-up, making sure issues are tracked, escalated and resolved in line with contractual terms

• Build global contract templates, playbooks and governance processes that work consistently across countries

• Monitor contract performance and compliance, flagging risks and improvement opportunities

• Be the go-to contact for the country teams and the wider operations organisation on contract questions and disputes

You will work with the country operations teams, Strategic Commercial Management (which owns PPAs, power trading and balancing contracts), Technical Operations, Investor Administration, SCADA Operations, Legal, Finance, and suppliers and service providers. Your role is to strengthen the countries' ability to manage contracts locally, not to add another layer of bureaucracy.

What we offer

You will join Global Operations at a time where we are transforming how we manage and operate our global asset portfolio. You will get a broad international scope, close collaboration across functions and countries, and the opportunity to work with complex commercial and operational challenges. We offer a high level of autonomy, a strong professional environment and the opportunity to make a visible impact on how Eurowind operates.

• A newly created role where you set the structures and ways of working

• The chance to make a real impact on how we improve and operate our commercial mindset

• Ownership, trust and room to shape your own area

• A global role with some travel, in an international and energetic environment

• A workplace in Hobro, alongside our operations colleagues

You will join a newly established team and report to Louise Guldager Thomsen, Head of Global Commercial Management. Louise is a collaborative and pragmatic leader who builds strong relationships, creates alignment across functions and empowers people to take ownership. She combines a deep understanding of the organisation with a practical focus on execution and a global perspective.

Required competencies and skills

You have solid experience with contract management, commercial agreements, warranties and/or claims, ideally from the energy, infrastructure, construction or other asset-intensive industries. You are comfortable navigating complex contractual matters and working across technical, commercial and legal topics. You combine strong analytical and negotiation skills with a pragmatic approach and the ability to turn contractual knowledge into action and business value.

• Significant experience in contract management within energy, infrastructure, renewables or another asset-intensive industry

• A proven record of leading complex contract negotiations end-to-end, including service and O&M, warranty, grid/curtailment, insurance and supplier contracts

• Solid understanding of commercial and legal risk management, with experience building or applying compliance frameworks

• Relevant legal, commercial or technical education (for example law, business or engineering), or equivalent hands-on experience

• International experience and comfort working across countries and cultures

• Enjoys building something new and setting up structures from scratch

• Works autonomously across a global organisation and values being part of a team

• Structured and detail-oriented, yet pragmatic about getting things done without unnecessary process

• Communicates clearly and directly, holding suppliers and internal stakeholders accountable while working with respect

Please note that this role requires a clean criminal record.

Renewable energy is our future. And so are our people!

At Eurowind Energy we do our best to create a culture where everyone is valued and feels at home. You will notice this in your everyday work life, where you have the freedom to speak up and where your voice means something to us. We know that when you grow, we grow. Therefore, we strive to support you in what you believe is right and in your personal and professional development. We offer you an exciting job in an energetic and international environment. And we promise you: the wind is never standing still.

Developing, operating and managing wind and solar parks is not just pure business for us. It is a way to view the world. And with this worldview comes a genuine ambition to be one of the leading developers in Europe. Because creating a future run entirely on green energy matters to us.

We manage our own portfolio of projects and at the same time, we perform technical and financial management of projects. We have throughout many years experienced sustained economic growth in the number of developed projects and companies in management. And we continue to expect this. Simply because it is in our nature to keep developing – projects, companies and our people.

Read more about Eurowind Energy A/S on our website or LinkedIn
